introduction.heading: Plumbing for Midvale homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Midvale were built in 1987 or later, and about 40% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Many of those homes are reaching the age when water heaters, faucets and fixtures need replacing. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

West Midvale gets its water from city-owned wells, and east Midvale gets water the city buys from the Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District. Hardness of the east side's water averaged 182 mg/L, according to the Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District's 2025 water quality report (no figure is published for the city wells). The U.S. Geological Survey classes that as very hard water. Hard water leaves mineral deposits in water heaters, faucets and appliances, and a water softener or filtration system cuts that buildup.

Midvale says its water system has no lead or galvanized service lines needing replacement; it checked service lines at buildings built before 1990 to finish its inventory.
